question: How do we make the top customers endpoint fast?
context: GET /stats/top-customers ranks customers by paid revenue over the last 30 days. It scans about 200,000 orders on every call and is slow under load. The sales dashboard polls it, and account managers use it right after closing large orders, so results must not lag far behind new orders.

baseline.name: Today (no change)
baseline.description: The code as it is now.

options.name: Cache
options.description: Cache the endpoint's response in memory with a 60 second time to live.

options.name: Materialized view
options.description: Precompute the ranking in a Postgres materialized view and refresh it in the background every 5 seconds.

options.name: Index and rewrite
options.description: Add the right index or indexes and rewrite the query so Postgres does less work. No caching and no precomputed tables.

diff.patch:
diff --git a/demo/orders-api/src/db.ts b/demo/orders-api/src/db.ts
index fa3c0a9..37e1b4d 100644
--- a/demo/orders-api/src/db.ts
+++ b/demo/orders-api/src/db.ts
@@ -38,4 +38,13 @@ export async function openDb(): Promise<PGlite> {
     FROM generate_series(1, ${ORDERS});
 
+    -- Partial covering index: filters to paid rows only (eliminating ~25% of
+    -- the table at index level), uses created_at as the leading column so the
+    -- 30-day range scan touches only the relevant slice, and includes
+    -- customer_id + amount_cents so Postgres can satisfy the GROUP BY / SUM
+    -- entirely from the index without visiting the heap (index-only scan).
+    CREATE INDEX orders_paid_created_customer_amount
+      ON orders (created_at DESC, customer_id, amount_cents)
+      WHERE status = 'paid';
+
     ANALYZE;
   `);

verdict.headline: Materialized view meets every constraint with the smallest change.
verdict.reason: Materialized view: p95 46.9 ms, 61 lines of code changed, 0 new dependencies. Cache fails staleness (60 s, needs ≤ 15 s); Index and rewrite fails p95 latency (235.6 ms, needs ≤ 50 ms).
